title: Signals for component state, not manual RxJS subscribe/unsubscribe
statement: Local component state is held in `signal()`/`computed()`, updated through `.set()`/`.update()`. A component does not `.subscribe()` to a stream to assign a plain field and then manage an `ngOnDestroy` unsubscribe by hand when a signal-based alternative (`toSignal`, or a signal fed by an existing API surface) is available.
rationale: Manual subscriptions are a real, common leak source: a forgotten `ngOnDestroy`/`takeUntil` keeps the subscription (and everything it closes over) alive past the component's lifetime. Signals have no subscription to forget, and pair directly with OnPush (QS-NG-009): a signal write is exactly the kind of change OnPush is designed to notice. `review-panel.ts` holds its entire local state - over a dozen fields - as signals with no manual subscription anywhere in the file.

good.caption: Local state as signals; no subscription to manage.

bad.caption: Manually managed subscription and plain-field state, easy to forget to unsubscribe.

changelog.summary: Initial rule, grounded in review-panel.ts's exclusively signal-based local state.
